correctness.rationale: If two deleted matched pairs were wholly omitted, their same-side vertices would have identical signatures. Hence at least n−1 pair indices are represented, and equality in size forces a one-hole transversal with omitted index h. If exactly one A vertex a_i is selected, its signature equals that of a_i b_h; if exactly two A vertices a_i,a_j are selected, it equals that of a_i b_j. Symmetrically any nonempty side must have size at least three. For a balanced transversal, covered indices of the oriented edge a_i b_j are decoded by its 0 or 2 entries (the shore determines the orientation), with a missing exceptional coordinate indicating h. This distinguishes all edges. Selected vertices have a zero and at least two twos on their own side, while an edge with that zero has at most one two on that side. Unselected vertices with a selected mate have a unique three, and the two omitted vertices have twos on opposite landmark sides, at least three twos each, unlike an edge. The same decoding for a one-sided transversal works when its sole side has at least three, since even an edge through h has a non-one entry; the omitted vertices are then all-ones and all-twos. Such a one-sided transversal cannot dominate its omitted vertex on the selected side. Balanced ones dominate, with a split possible iff n>=7. For n=3..6 a full side gives a size-n witness by the signature rules, including one distinct three per vertex on the opposite side. The stable count is n times the number of orientations of n−1 indices excluding assignments with 0, 1 or 2 on either side, giving n(2^(n−1)−n²+n−2).
residual_risks: The recorded exhaustive comparison is bounded to n=3..9; proof, not finite output, supports the all-n claim. No complete transition-case basis enumeration is asserted.

evidence: Mixed resolution implies vertex resolution and both signs for any adjacent pair (compare each endpoint with the edge). A same-side difference has at most two coordinates of either nonzero sign, so cannot be constant on a mixed set of at least three unless the pair is unresolved. A mixed set of size at most two cannot occur: n>=4 requires at least n−1 indices, and at n=3 the one-hole two-vertex candidates fail the endpoint-versus-edge test.

For a matched nonedge represented in S, its coordinate −3 or +3 is unique. If the pair is unrepresented, domination forces S to meet both shores, giving differences 1 and −1. Thus any mixed resolving dominating S is doubly resolving, which transfers the published lower bound and the necessity of its stable optimum structure.

Conversely every stable doubly resolving basis from 8416a7acedbc is a balanced one-hole transversal; these dominate, their edges resolve by b5b3c45f23e8 or the endpoint-index decoding, and the nonincident vertex-edge checks are immediate from the zero, unique-three, and at-least-three-twos criteria. Incident pairs already separate by the two-sign condition. A full shore dominates and mixed-resolves in the small sizes by direct signatures, attaining the prior lower bound.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The reduction transfers the entire finding, including the exact family and count (not merely the stable scalar). A distinction between the definitions remains for other sets, and transition-case MRD enumerations might differ from doubly resolving ones, but the frozen finding does not give such an enumeration.

originality.rationale: A distinct published Resultary record, 8416a7acedbc, gives exactly the same optimum values and stable minimizing families for doubly resolving sets of the same crown graphs. This is verified coverage by implication, not just a numerical match or same-day priority assertion: every mixed resolving dominating set in a crown graph is doubly resolving, and all of that record's stable optimal doubly resolving bases are mixed resolving and dominating. For n=3..6 the full-shore witness supplies the upper bound matching the same record's lower bound. The related edge-only crown bases result supplies the edge separation directly, leaving only elementary vertex-edge signature checks to transfer the stable family.
residual_risks: Priority order between the distinct same-day findings was not established. The positive coverage judgment rests on mathematical implication from the available statement, not on inferring that order.
Coverage of crown graphs or their n=3 cycle by the introducing paper remains unverified.
